title: I’ve Been Under A Rock. Why Is TikTok A National Security Threat, But Jensen Huang Is Fine?
excerpt: Hello, I have been living under a rock for the last twelve years. Can you help me understand the United States’ current views on tech policy and foreign affairs? Oh boy. You’ve missed a…
content_html:
from the a-little-q-and-a dept

Hello, I have been living under a rock for the last twelve years. Can you help me understand the United States’ current views on tech policy and foreign affairs?

Oh boy. You’ve missed a lot. Okay, here in the second Donald Trump administration, China is clearly our biggest enemy and threat. Indeed, it’s such a huge threat that a bipartisan group of folks got together during the Biden administration (which happened between the two Trump administrations) to ban the Chinese social media site TikTok.

Oh wow. What is this TikTok anyway? Was it being used by the Chinese to conduct surveillance on Americans?

Not that anyone has ever been able to prove! It’s an app used by teens to share quick videos of themselves dancing. And sometimes they comment on the news.

Wait. And this is a problem?

Yes! As Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said while negotiating the forced sale of TikTok to US interests, the US is “not willing to sacrifice national security interests for a social media app.” Indeed, back when he was a Senator introducing one of the bills to ban TikTok if it stayed Chinese-owned, now-Secretary of State Marco Rubio made it quite clear: “We know it answers to the People’s Republic of China. There is no more time to waste on meaningless negotiations with a CCP-puppet company. It is time to ban Beijing-controlled TikTok for good.”

Wow. China must really be a serious threat to American tech interests. I assume we’re also banning the sale of our top-line semiconductors to China?

Well, about that… technically, we are banning the most sophisticated GPUs (necessary for building advanced artificial intelligence systems) to China, but Trump keeps allowing the leading GPU company, Nvidia, to sell its GPUs to China.

I assume they’re pretty careful about who those go to, though?

Well, you see, the founder and CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, got caught in an alleged honeypot scheme with an alleged Chinese spy, who was running a front company in Singapore that supposedly helped funnel way more GPUs into China.

That’s crazy! Has he been arrested?

Oh no. He briefly resigned (after admitting to the affair, plus two more — though he now admits it was way more than that). But then Donald Trump called into an Nvidia board meeting and convinced them to rehire Huang.

They… rehired him? The President? Called into a board meeting?

Oh yes. That’s how we do business in the US these days. The President considers it his duty to help rich cheating oligarchs who say nice things about him.

But does this mean he was illegally funneling strategically important technology to “our biggest enemy” at a time when we cannot “sacrifice national security”?

That’s cute. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says it’s no big deal because the chips weren’t going to the Chinese military, just to companies that work with the Chinese military — companies like Alibaba, which he described as mostly a social media company.

Isn’t he the same guy who said he wasn’t willing to sacrifice national security over a social media app? And didn’t Rubio say that TikTok answers to the People’s Republic of China? Would Alibaba do that too?

Sorry, were you expecting consistency? I guess now is the point I should mention that Jensen Huang also has been a prolific contributor to various Donald Trump extravagances, which appears to have bought him quite a lot of goodwill.

Surely someone in the administration is keeping an eye on this?

Well, yes, that’s the job of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under fire for helping Huang and Nvidia sell more chips to China (did I mention the firm Lutnick ran for years, which is now run by his sons, has extensive ties to Nvidia?)

Wait, how is he still a cabinet member?

Actually, that’s a funny story! When Trump reportedly considered firing him over his ties to deceased underage sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein (also formerly Trump’s best friend), Lutnick donated $25 million to Trump’s Presidential library, which Trump asked Lutnick for directly. Indeed, it’s been reported that Trump brags that the only reason he keeps Lutnick around is the money he donated.

That all seems unbelievable. Doesn’t the US have laws to stop this kind of threat from foreign adversaries trying to corruptly influence our important tech supply chains?

Yes, but these days we only use them to threaten American companies that don’t allow the Fox News weekend anchor Trump put in charge of the Pentagon to use their AI services to launch autonomous attacks on brown people. That’s considered a “supply chain risk.” Having sex with (alleged) Chinese spies and blowing past export restrictions to ship our most powerful GPUs to China is just the cost of keeping the stock market artificially inflated.

Doesn’t that seem way more risky?

Sure, but risk isn’t really the point. It’s all part of Donald Trump’s rejection of capitalism, in favor of state control over industry, a la China.

Wait, the Republican Party now supports state control of businesses?

Yes! Trump regularly makes efforts to nationalize and control American business. Though, ironically, their entire argument during the midterm election was that it was the Democrats who were communists.

How did that work out?

Not well. Democrats swept Congress in record-breaking ways (not to mention many other races around the country) even after Elon Musk spent nearly half a billion dollars trying to get Republicans elected.

Elon Musk? The electric car guy? I would have thought he was a liberal darling for pushing alternative energy?

You really have missed a lot. Elon Musk has gone all in for fascism. Oh, and that includes supporting Russia in their war against Ukraine (ostensibly an American ally) by degrading the satellite technology he provides to make sure Ukraine can’t easily defend itself against Russian attacks.

Excuse me, what?

Yeah, it’s been a lot.

So, to summarize, we tried banning the Chinese social media dancing app for “national security” reasons and punishing an American AI company because it won’t let the US indiscriminately use AI to kill people… but at the same time the President and his cabinet are interfering in private company governance to allow the guy who slept with an (alleged) Chinese spy and dodged export controls to give powerful computer chips to our biggest enemy, China, while the electric car guy is freely able to fiddle with satellite technology to prevent an American ally from defending itself against another enemy of the US, Russia?

Yeah, that’s pretty much the deal. I guess now is when I should mention that Donald Trump also is deeply invested in Nvidia to the tune of tens of millions of dollars, so he’s profiting from this mess. And, also that he called Russian leader Vladimir Putin his friend, even as Putin continues waging war on Ukraine and has spent decades working against the United States and its allies.

I’m going back under the rock.

Wait! We didn’t even get to Trump demanding Intel’s CEO get fired due to his close ties to China… until Intel handed 10% of the company to the Trump administration. Or how the UAE got access to AI chips as well after investing $500 million in a sketchy Trump family venture, with a huge percentage of that money going directly to the Trump family. Or how Trump only allowed Nvidia and AMD to sell chips to China after the US government was told it would get 15% of any revenue (later bumped to 25% for some chips). There’s so much more! We’ve barely started!

Leave me alone! This timeline is ridiculous!

Companies: anthropic, nvidia, spacex, tiktok

from the a-little-q-and-a dept

Hello, I have been living under a rock for the last twelve years. Can you help me understand the United States’ current views on tech policy and foreign affairs?

噢，孩子。 You’ve missed a lot. Okay, here in the second Donald Trump administration, China is clearly our biggest enemy and threat. Indeed, it’s such a huge threat that a bipartisan group of folks got together during the Biden administration (which happened between the two Trump administrations) to ban the Chinese social media site TikTok.

哦哇。 What is this TikTok anyway? Was it being used by the Chinese to conduct surveillance on Americans?

Not that anyone has ever been able to prove! It’s an app used by teens to share quick videos of themselves dancing. And sometimes they comment on the news.

等待。 And this is a problem?

是的！ As Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said while negotiating the forced sale of TikTok to US interests, the US is “not willing to sacrifice national security interests for a social media app.” Indeed, back when he was a Senator introducing one of the bills to ban TikTok if it stayed Chinese-owned, now-Secretary of State Marco Rubio made it quite clear: “We know it answers to the People’s Republic of China. There is no more time to waste on meaningless negotiations with a CCP-puppet company. It is time to ban Beijing-controlled TikTok for good.”

哇。 China must really be a serious threat to American tech interests. I assume we’re also banning the sale of our top-line semiconductors to China?

Well, about that… technically, we are banning the most sophisticated GPUs (necessary for building advanced artificial intelligence systems) to China, but Trump keeps allowing the leading GPU company, Nvidia, to sell its GPUs to China.

I assume they’re pretty careful about who those go to, though?

Well, you see, the founder and CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, got caught in an alleged honeypot scheme with an alleged Chinese spy, who was running a front company in Singapore that supposedly helped funnel way more GPUs into China.

That’s crazy! Has he been arrested?

哦不。 He briefly resigned (after admitting to the affair, plus two more — though he now admits it was way more than that). But then Donald Trump called into an Nvidia board meeting and convinced them to rehire Huang.

They… rehired him? The President? Called into a board meeting?

Oh yes. That’s how we do business in the US these days. The President considers it his duty to help rich cheating oligarchs who say nice things about him.

But does this mean he was illegally funneling strategically important technology to “our biggest enemy” at a time when we cannot “sacrifice national security”?

That’s cute. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says it’s no big deal because the chips weren’t going to the Chinese military, just to companies that work with the Chinese military — companies like Alibaba, which he described as mostly a social media company.

Isn’t he the same guy who said he wasn’t willing to sacrifice national security over a social media app? And didn’t Rubio say that TikTok answers to the People’s Republic of China? Would Alibaba do that too?

Sorry, were you expecting consistency? I guess now is the point I should mention that Jensen Huang also has been a prolific contributor to various Donald Trump extravagances, which appears to have bought him quite a lot of goodwill.

Surely someone in the administration is keeping an eye on this?

Well, yes, that’s the job of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under fire for helping Huang and Nvidia sell more chips to China (did I mention the firm Lutnick ran for years, which is now run by his sons, has extensive ties to Nvidia?)

Wait, how is he still a cabinet member?

Actually, that’s a funny story! When Trump reportedly considered firing him over his ties to deceased underage sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein (also formerly Trump’s best friend), Lutnick donated $25 million to Trump’s Presidential library, which Trump asked Lutnick for directly. Indeed, it’s been reported that Trump brags that the only reason he keeps Lutnick around is the money he donated.

That all seems unbelievable. Doesn’t the US have laws to stop this kind of threat from foreign adversaries trying to corruptly influence our important tech supply chains?

Yes, but these days we only use them to threaten American companies that don’t allow the Fox News weekend anchor Trump put in charge of the Pentagon to use their AI services to launch autonomous attacks on brown people. That’s considered a “supply chain risk.” Having sex with (alleged) Chinese spies and blowing past export restrictions to ship our most powerful GPUs to China is just the cost of keeping the stock market artificially inflated.

Doesn’t that seem way more risky?

Sure, but risk isn’t really the point. It’s all part of Donald Trump’s rejection of capitalism, in favor of state control over industry, a la China.

Wait, the Republican Party now supports state control of businesses?

是的！ Trump regularly makes efforts to nationalize and control American business. Though, ironically, their entire argument during the midterm election was that it was the Democrats who were communists.

How did that work out?

Not well. Democrats swept Congress in record-breaking ways (not to mention many other races around the country) even after Elon Musk spent nearly half a billion dollars trying to get Republicans elected.

Elon Musk? The electric car guy? I would have thought he was a liberal darling for pushing alternative energy?

You really have missed a lot. Elon Musk has gone all in for fascism. Oh, and that includes supporting Russia in their war against Ukraine (ostensibly an American ally) by degrading the satellite technology he provides to make sure Ukraine can’t easily defend itself against Russian attacks.

Excuse me, what?

Yeah, it’s been a lot.

So, to summarize, we tried banning the Chinese social media dancing app for “national security” reasons and punishing an American AI company because it won’t let the US indiscriminately use AI to kill people… but at the same time the President and his cabinet are interfering in private company governance to allow the guy who slept with an (alleged) Chinese spy and dodged export controls to give powerful computer chips to our biggest enemy, China, while the electric car guy is freely able to fiddle with satellite technology to prevent an American ally from defending itself against another enemy of the US, Russia?

Yeah, that’s pretty much the deal. I guess now is when I should mention that Donald Trump also is deeply invested in Nvidia to the tune of tens of millions of dollars, so he’s profiting from this mess. And, also that he called Russian leader Vladimir Putin his friend, even as Putin continues waging war on Ukraine and has spent decades working against the United States and its allies.

I’m going back under the rock.

等待！ We didn’t even get to Trump demanding Intel’s CEO get fired due to his close ties to China… until Intel handed 10% of the company to the Trump administration. Or how the UAE got access to AI chips as well after investing $500 million in a sketchy Trump family venture, with a huge percentage of that money going directly to the Trump family. Or how Trump only allowed Nvidia and AMD to sell chips to China after the US government was told it would get 15% of any revenue (later bumped to 25% for some chips). There’s so much more! We’ve barely started!

Leave me alone! This timeline is ridiculous!
